title: "Bonds : Time and Rate Sensitivity — Review"

# Forward Rates (Forward Rates)

## Definition & Key Formula

**Forward rate** : interest rate implicitly contained in the zero-coupon curve for a future period.

$$\boxed{r_{T_1, T_2} = \frac{R_2 T_2 - R_1 T_1}{T_2 - T_1}}$$

- $R_1, R_2$ : zero-coupon rates at maturities $T_1 < T_2$
- Convention : **continuous compounding**

## No-Arbitrage Logic

Two equivalent strategies over 2 years → same final result :

| Strategy | Calculation |
|:----------|:-------|
| Invest 2 years directly | $100 \cdot e^{R_2 \cdot 2}$ |
| Invest 1 year + forward 1y1 | $100 \cdot e^{R_1} \cdot e^{r_{1,2}}$ |

→ If $r_{1,2}$ deviates → **arbitrage possible** (risk-free profit).

## Numerical Example

| Maturity | Zero rate (%) | Forward rate next year (%) |
|:--------:|:-------------:|:-------------------------------:|
| 1 year     | 10,0          | —                               |
| 2 years    | 10,5          | **11,0**                        |
| 3 years    | 10,8          | **11,4**                        |

Calculation 1y1 : $\frac{0{,}105 \times 2 - 0{,}10 \times 1}{1} = 11\%$

::: {.callout-tip title="Practical application"}
**Future mortgage** : loan in 1 year for 10 years → banker uses rates at **1 year** and **11 years**.
:::

# Yield Curve Evolution (Yield Curve Evolution)

| Movement | Description | Economic Signal |
|:----------|:------------|:------------------|
| **Parallel shift** (Parallel shift) | All rates move by the same amount | Uniform monetary policy |
| **Flattening** (Flattening) | Short rates ↑ and/or long rates ↓ | Slowdown anticipated |
| **Steepening** (Steepening) | Short rates ↓ and/or long rates ↑ | Recovery anticipated |

::: {.callout-note title="Key takeaway"}
- **Short** end of the curve → driven by **central banks**
- **Long** end → driven by the **market**
:::

# Duration (Duration)

## Definition — Macaulay Duration

$$\boxed{D = \sum_{i=1}^{n} (t_i - t) \cdot \frac{c_i \, e^{-y(t_i-t)}}{B(t)}}$$

→ Weighted average of payment dates (weights = relative present value of each cash flow).

| Bond Type | Duration |
|:------------------|:---------|
| Zero-coupon, maturity $n$ | $D = n$ |
| Coupon-bearing bond, maturity $n$ | $D < n$ |

## Duration–price relation ⚠️

$$\boxed{\frac{\delta B}{B} \approx -D \cdot \delta y}$$

- Rate rise ($\delta y > 0$) → **price fall**
- High duration → **strong sensitivity**

## Numerical Validation (example 10 %, 3 years, yield 12 %)

| Parameter | Value |
|:----------|:------:|
| Price $B$ | 94,213 USD |
| Duration $D$ | 2,653 years |

For $\delta y = 0{,}1\%$ → estimate = reality = **−0,250 USD** ✓

For $\delta y = 1{,}0\%$ → estimate = −2,499 USD ≠ actual = −2,464 USD ⚠️

---

# Convexity (Convexity)

## Formula

$$\boxed{C = \frac{1}{B}\frac{\partial^2 B}{\partial y^2} = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{c_i \, t_i^2 \, e^{-y(t_i-t)}}{B}}$$

## 2nd-order approximation

$$\boxed{\frac{\delta B}{B} \approx -D \cdot \delta y + \frac{1}{2} C \cdot (\delta y)^2}$$

For $\delta y = 1\%$, $C = 7{,}570$ → exact result = **−2,464 USD** ✓

::: {.callout-important title="Common pitfall"}
**Duration alone underestimates** the impact of a large rate shock. Always add convexity for $|\delta y| \geq 0{,}5\%$.

Convexity is **favorable** to the holder : smaller losses / larger gains than linearly predicted.
:::

---

# Types of Duration

| Type | Formula | Usage |
|:-----|:--------|:------|
| **Macaulay** | $D = \sum w_i \cdot t_i$ | Interest rate risk measure |
| **Modified** (Modified) | $D_{\text{mod}} = \dfrac{D}{1 + y/n_c}$ | Relative rate sensitivity |
| **Dollar / DV01** | $\text{DV01} = \dfrac{D_{\text{mod}} \cdot B}{100}$ | Portfolio management |
| **Effective** | Adjusted for embedded options | Callable / putable bonds |
| **Key Rate** (Key Rate) | Sensitivity by curve segment | Non-parallel shocks |

---

# Portfolio Management

$$D_{\text{portfolio}} = \sum_k w_k \cdot D_k$$

- **Rising rates** → reduce duration (sell long, buy short)
- **Falling rates** → increase duration
- Duration ≈ good **volatility proxy** of the portfolio
- Multi-currency portfolio → duration calculated **by currency**

# Formulas to Remember Absolutely

| Formula | Meaning |
|:--------|:--------------|
| $r = \dfrac{R_2 T_2 - R_1 T_1}{T_2 - T_1}$ | Forward rate between $T_1$ and $T_2$ |
| $\dfrac{\partial B}{\partial y} = -B \cdot D$ | Price/rate derivative |
| $\dfrac{\delta B}{B} \approx -D \cdot \delta y$ | 1st-order approximation |
| $\dfrac{\delta B}{B} \approx -D \cdot \delta y + \dfrac{1}{2}C(\delta y)^2$ | 2nd-order approximation |
| $D_{\text{mod}} = \dfrac{D}{1 + y/n_c}$ | Modified duration |
| $\text{DV01} = \dfrac{D_{\text{mod}} \cdot B}{100}$ | Dollar duration |
